verses.ar:
Name and title: Abu Abd Allah Malik ibn Anas al-Asbahi, the Imam of Medina and founder of the Maliki school of law.
Born: about 93 AH (711 CE), Medina; sources give dates between 93 and 97 AH.
Died: 179 AH (795 CE), Medina.
Teachers: Nafi, the freed servant of Ibn Umar; Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri; Yahya ibn Said al-Ansari; Rabia ibn Abi Abd al-Rahman (Rabi'at al-Ra'y).
Students: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafii, Muhammad al-Shaybani, Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Qasim, Abd Allah ibn Wahb and Yahya ibn Yahya al-Laythi.
Works: al-Muwatta, one of the earliest books of hadith and law.

Malik was born in Medina into a family of scholars and spent almost his whole life in the city of the Prophet ﷺ, leaving only to perform Hajj. He studied hadith and jurisprudence with the scholars of Medina, above all Nafi, the freed servant of Ibn Umar, and Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri, and he began to give legal opinions and teach in the Prophet's Mosque, where students came from across the Muslim world. He was known for his respect for hadith and for the city, and it is related that he would sit to teach only after washing and wearing his best clothes, out of reverence for the words of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. He passed away in Medina in 179 AH and is buried in al-Baqi.

His great book, al-Muwatta, composed in the second half of the 2nd century AH, gathers the hadith of the Prophet ﷺ, the sayings of the Companions and the successors, and the established practice of the people of Medina, arranged by the chapters of the law; al-Shafii is reported to have called it among the soundest of books after the Book of Allah. Malik gave great weight to the continuous practice of Medina, which he regarded as an inheritance passed down from the Companions who lived beside the Prophet ﷺ, and his method was carried by his students to Egypt, North Africa and al-Andalus, where the Maliki school remains strong today. He was also known for his caution in giving fatwa, saying “I do not know” when he did not know, which scholars hold up as an example of the humility of the people of knowledge.
